last_key_points: Crude reversed higher after the prior evening memo, with Brent around 98.16 and WTI around 99.15 as traders re-priced persistent physical disruption despite the ceasefire headline.
Hormuz remained functionally restricted rather than normalized, with Reuters describing traffic as near standstill and OSINT shipping trackers showing sparse, abnormal routing.
Pakistan became the clearest live diplomatic channel, with NBC reporting active mediation and Islamabad showing visible security preparations for expected U.S.-Iran talks.
Lebanon remained the main ceasefire spoiler theater as fresh Israeli strikes kept regional escalation risk elevated even without renewed direct U.S.-Iran fire.
Regional energy infrastructure risk broadened beyond the strait itself, including reported threats to Saudi bypass infrastructure and unverified but notable claims of damage at a Dubai fuel site.
